newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00 cent higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00 cent higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 1.00 cent higher Wednesday despite a build-up in CSCE certified coffee stocks and an increase in stocks pending certification, dealers said.
After Tuesday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks rose 1,783 60-kg bags as of June 30 to 49,900 bags. There were 27,313 bags pending grading.
New York arabica futures ended higher but well below peaks Tuesday as latest Brazilian weather forecasts called for favorable weather through the weekend.
"There is no damaging cold weather indicated during the next seven days," Weather Service Corp said.
September settled up 2.85 cents at 175.25 cents a lb after ranging from 184.50 to 173.00. Spot July finished 4.10 cents higher at 196.50 cents, while the outer months gained 2.25 to 3.34 cents.
The July/September switch widened to 21.25 cents, from 20.00 cents at the close on Monday, while September/December narrowed to 20.90 cents compared with 21.50 cents.
Technically, traders pegged near-term September support at Tuesday's low of 173.00 cents, with resistance seen near 184.50 to 185.00 cents, followed by 192.00.

Brazilian coffee exporters Tuesday were monitoring a strike at the key port of Santos but said the stoppage had come at a quiet time for coffee shipments, and would only effect coffee if it continued beyond a couple of days.
The strike, which began on Tuesday, involves 800 administrative portworkers who are protesting against not being consulted about the port's switch to 24-hour operations, due to have begun on June 30.
Players will also monitor the effects of Monday's volcano eruption in Mexico, as damage to coffee-growing regions is yet unknown.
London robusta futures were higher early Wednesday but volume remained light ahead of the Independence Day holiday in the United States. The New York market will be closed on Friday, July 4.

At the midday break, benchmark LIFFE September was up $5 to the session high of $1,826, while November rose $4 to $1,810. Volume focused on light industry buying, switches and some book squaring, industry sources said.
